create.title: Uniform pointwise bound for the direct actual-profile kernel
create.statement_tex: Let H^prof_(T,X)(h,q) be the exact Round-15 actual-profile scale sum: complete height inversion on Re v=b>0, complete interior spatial inversions, and symmetric top spatial truncation of W_+hat(u)=1/u+R_W(u), with all floors, Phi factors, fixed profiles, and endpoint stars retained. Then sup_(T,h,q)|H^prof_(T,X)(h,q)|<<_W log(2X). The sharp 1/u part is bounded by symmetric sine-integral/Dirichlet inversion and has values 1,1/2,0 at the limiting Perron projector; R_W and interior transforms are uniformly bounded per scale, and there are O(log X) scales. No absolute integration of 1/u is used.
create.next_action: Use only for the pre-functional-equation physical profile or another kernel proved exactly equal to it; do not attach it to the reflected Hankel remainder.

create.title: The post-functional-equation remainder is not an accepted scalar incidence kernel
create.statement_tex: After finite-height radial functional-equation reflection and residue subtraction, the non-residue term retains G_v(1-s)K_(u+v)(1-s)F_(-(u+v))(s), finite horizontal sides, and a new dual radial index after expanding the Dirichlet series. The gamma quotient couples s to u+v and the radial transform couples s to v and the finite square-root-wave cutoff. No accepted inverse produces a bounded scalar H_(T,X)(h,q), an algebraic delta at the original incidence, or a uniform triple-height L1 majorant. Hence the Round-16 schematic scalar post-FE kernel is not well-formed as a pointwise multiplier; it must be replaced by a vector kernel K_(T,X)(h,q;m) or the original three-contour operator, with all residues kept separately.
create.next_action: Formulate the surviving reflected remainder as a vector-valued Hankel kernel or finite three-contour operator and audit uniform large-complex-shift localization before estimating it.

create.title: Uniform vector-valued reflected Hankel kernel estimate
create.statement_tex: With every zeta, height, spatial-Perron, and radial endpoint residue listed outside, define the finite post-functional-equation vector kernel K_(T,X)(h,q;m) by the joint u,v,s integral containing G_v(1-s)K_(u+v)(1-s), the actual scale/floor/profile factors, and finite horizontal sides. Prove a target-sized operator or signed correlation estimate uniform in all three contour heights and large Im(u+v), sufficient for the reflected maximal angular problem. A scalar pointwise profile estimate does not imply this theorem.
create.next_action: Derive a finite explicit formula and phase diagram for the vector Hankel kernel; separate terminal/horizontal sides before considering a large-shift theorem or source search.

update.rejection_reason: The full post-FE object is vector-valued in a dual radial index and is not defined as a scalar H_(T,X)(h,q); only the direct physical profile has the proved pointwise bound.
update.next_action: Use M9-M1-direct-profile-kernel-pointwise-bound for direct profiles and replace the full reflected scalar claim by M9-M1-post-FE-vector-kernel.

update.statement_tex: The divisor estimate with v_2(hq)>=K is <<B_X N_X^(1/4)2^(-K)log(2N_X) for any genuine scalar incidence kernel bounded pointwise by B_X. It is unconditional for the direct profile H^prof, using B_X<<log X. It does not apply to the full post-FE remainder, which is a vector Hankel kernel; a corresponding high-2-adic operator tail remains conditional on M9-M1-post-FE-vector-kernel.
update.next_action: Do not remove the high-2-adic part of the reflected remainder until a vector-kernel norm or signed operator estimate is proved.

update.statement_tex: The direct actual-profile part has a scalar O(log X) kernel and exact local reflection projection. After radial functional-equation reflection, however, the non-residue remainder is the vector-valued joint u,v,s Hankel kernel M9-M1-post-FE-vector-kernel, with all zeta, height, hard-top Perron, and radial endpoint residues outside. Prove a target-sized signed operator estimate for this vector remainder and every residue; no scalar pointwise H_(T,X)(h,q) formulation is accepted.
update.next_action: Derive the explicit finite vector Hankel kernel, its contour/phase ranges and horizontal sides; only then select a large-shift analytic theorem or a new cancellation mechanism.

reject.reason: The reflected gamma/radial transform has a new dual index and joint s,u,v dependence, not a scalar multiplier of the original incidence.
Symmetric sine-integral inversion bounds only the bare physical profile; it gives no uniform estimate for the coupled gamma quotient, radial transform, or finite horizontal sides.
Subtracting zeta, height, Perron, and endpoint residues leaves the nonseparable Hankel operator; the zeta residue is itself global in the radial variable.
The direct profile bound proves a direct-profile tail only; the full post-FE high-2-adic component is vector-valued and remains conditional.

no_change.reason: No uniform vector Hankel or target-sized global estimate was proved.
Round 18 concerns transformed M1 kernel formalization.
Kernel formalization and an obstruction do not prove the target.

round_assessment.reason: Round 18 proves the direct scalar Perron/profile bound but catches a category error in the reflected formulation: the survivor is a vector Hankel operator, not a scalar incidence weight. It prevents an invalid tail promotion and identifies the exact next analytic object.
